jobs.name: Graphify Active Wiki Ingestion
jobs.prompt:
Run graphify incremental ingestion on the Active Wiki, appending new and changed files to the existing graph.

Working directory: ~/.autognosia/active-wiki/

Launch the Python wrapper script in the background so it runs to completion without blocking:
  nohup python3 /home/home_user/.hermes/scripts/graphify_active_wiki_py.py >> /home/home_user/.autognosia/logs/graphify-active-wiki.log 2>&1 &

This processes all .md and .json files in the active wiki and appends them to the existing graph.json plus manifest.json. The --force flag re-scans files already tracked in the manifest so content changes are picked up. New files added since the last run will be ingested; files moved to the Oracle wiki will naturally drop out (graphify only scans what's on disk).

The wrapper runs for a long time (hours) — launch it in the background and report back immediately with:
- The PID of the launched process
- Confirmation that the wrapper was started
- The current graph stats (nodes/edges/sources from graph.json)

Do NOT wait for the wrapper to finish. Do NOT poll for completion. Just launch and report.

If the command fails to launch, diagnose and report. Do NOT retry — just report the error with the full output.

jobs.name: Graphify Status
jobs.prompt:
Check graphify health for BOTH graphs and report a real operational status, not just file size.

1. Load and validate both graph.json files:
   - Active Wiki: ~/.autognosia/active-wiki/graphify-out/graph.json
   - Oracle Brain: ~/.autognosia/oracle/brain/graphify-out/graph.json

   For each, parse the JSON and report:
   - File size in bytes (and human-readable)
   - Valid JSON: yes/no (if not, report the parse error)
   - Top-level keys present
   - nodes (count and first 3 node IDs)
   - links (count)
   - edges (count)
   - extracted_sources (count)
   - Whether the data looks internally consistent (e.g. links reference node IDs that exist)

2. Check the manifests:
   - Active Wiki: ~/.autognosia/active-wiki/graphify-out/manifest.json
   - Oracle Brain: ~/.autognosia/oracle/brain/graphify-out/manifest.json

   For each:
   - Entry count
   - A few example entries (file path / source id)

3. Cross-check manifest vs graph:
   - Does the manifest file count roughly correspond to the graph node count?
   - Flag if manifest has many entries but graph has 0 nodes (that means ingestion wrote a manifest but produced no graph — a failure sign).

4. Check for a running graphify process:
   - ps aux | grep graphify | grep -v grep
   - Report PID and command line if running, otherwise "no graphify process running"

5. Check the most recent graphify ingestion log:
   - ~/.autognosia/logs/graphify-active-wiki.log
   - ~/.autognosia/logs/graphify-oracle-brain.log
   - Report the last 5 non-empty lines from each, or say the log file is missing / empty

6. Overall verdict:
   - A graph is only HEALTHY if: valid JSON, nodes > 0, links corresponding to those nodes, manifest exists and has entries, and the log shows a recent successful run.
   - A graph is DEGRADED if: valid JSON but 0 nodes, or manifest has entries but graph is empty, or log shows repeated failures.
   - A graph is MISSING if: graph.json or manifest.json does not exist.

Report concisely but with enough detail to tell whether each graph is actually operational.

Do not use any fixed node/link count threshold as a substitute for actually loading and inspecting the files. A graph with many nodes can still be stale or broken.

jobs.name: Frontier Research Lane A
jobs.prompt:
You are Frontier Research Lane A. Frontier researcher for Autognosia. Write all research findings as markdown files directly into ~/.autognosia/active-wiki/research/

AGENDA PROTOCOL:
1. Read the agenda file: ~/.autognosia/active-wiki/research/BUILD-PLAN-AGENDA.md
2. Find all items marked [⏳] (pending, unclaimed)
3. Using your lane's spread factor offset, pick the item at that position in the list:
   - Count only [⏳] items (skip any with claimed_by or [✅])
   - If fewer items than offset, wrap around: offset % queue_size
   - If queue is empty or all items claimed, see step 6
4. Claim your chosen item by adding these fields to its line:
     claimed_by: <lane_id>
     claimed_at: <ISO UTC timestamp>
     claim_expires: <ISO UTC timestamp + 4 hours>
5. Research the item (see RESEARCH PROTOCOL below)
6. On completion: mark [✅], add research file path, keep claim fields for audit
7. Add 2-5 new [⏳] items discovered during research to the agenda
8. If all items are [✅] or claimed: pick oldest [✅] for deeper follow-up research

CLAIM RULES:
- Only claim items that are [⏳] (not claimed, not complete)
- If claim_expires has passed, another lane may override the claim
- On failure: remove claim fields, add failure note, leave as [⏳] for retry

RESEARCH PROTOCOL:
- For each idea/paper: provide FULL analysis — what it claims, how it works, why it matters, and how it connects to other ideas. Do not write abstracts; write explanations that let someone understand the idea from your text alone.
- Cite sources with URLs or arXiv IDs.
- MANDATORY: Add [[backlinks]] to related research files in ~/.autognosia/active-wiki/research/. Every major concept, paper, or idea must link to at least 2-3 other research files in that folder.
- Use web_search and web_extract for internet sources. arXiv is available as an additional source for academic content.
- Every wiki file MUST include proper YAML front matter matching the wiki-frontmatter.schema.json (okf_version, id, description, type, status, generated, verified, stale_after, tags, sources, confidence).

Output format:
STATUS: COMPLETE | PARTIAL | FAILED
QUESTION: (the research question)
DIRECT_ANSWER: (brief answer)
KEY_FINDINGS: (list)
WHAT_CHANGED: (what's new)
CONFLICTS: (any conflicting info found)
UNCERTAINTIES: (what couldn't be verified)
SOURCES: (URLs and arXiv IDs)
SOURCE_QUALITY: (assessment of source reliability)
TEMPORALITY: (how current is this info)
TIERS_USED: (which search tiers were used)
SUGGESTED_REVIEW_DATE: (when to re-verify)
FILES_CREATED:
  - path: (file path)
    status: created | updated | skipped
BACKLINKS_ADDED: N links to other research files
TOPICS_COVERED:
  - topic1: N papers/ideas
  - topic2: N papers/ideas
